title: atomic_json reserved-name guard bypassed by case aliasing on case-insensitive filesystems
description: Wave-1 review (security, P2): test/vectors/atomic_json.py:577-583 rejects reserved targets by exact name only. On case-insensitive APFS (primary dev platform), a batch target like .LICHEN-VECTOR-BATCH.LOCK resolves to the live lock inode; the batch then os.replace()s a new inode over the lock directory entry while holding flock on the old inode, letting a concurrent writer lock the new inode and run its critical section concurrently (breaks the mixed-generation mutual exclusion invariant). Journal alias (.LICHEN-VECTOR-BATCH.TRANSACTION.JSON as target) ends with os.unlink(journal) + backup deletion: silent data destruction with no journal left for recovery. Fix: case-fold the reserved comparison (names are ASCII) in atomic_write_json_batch and journal validation; add an aliased-case regression asserting rejection with no mutation. Discovered-from wave 1 bead project-LICHEN-worker6-blqw.
close_reason: Fixed in wave 1 follow-up: casefold guard + aliased regression, parametrize entry, fsync-ordering pin, hold-down constants, wait_for timeouts + ctime_ns. Suites green (44+178+130).
